During a naval dispatch with loaded transports, assigned escorts retain their guard orders through the next escort refresh while non-escort warships receive and retain outbound attack orders.
Both percentage and town-size naval launches apply the configured naval attack percentage and return it to zero afterward.
A one-window naval loss is followed by a zero current-loss sample when fleet count stabilizes and does not repeatedly retrigger retreat behavior.

With at least two idle home-island villagers, civilian migration owns the next available utility transport instead of a retrying scout mission; scout attempts remain bounded even when no empty transport or viable landing is found.

Civilian boarding telemetry can request up to the researched transport capacity; a full load departs immediately, or after 45 seconds a partial load departs when at least two settlers have boarded, and unboarded villagers cease chasing a departed or lost hull.

On RIVERS, ISLANDS, and TEAM-ISLANDS classifications, the depleted-economy cleanup does not delete prospective passengers before migration can select them, and successful lifts can repeat after a 60-second rearm interval.

A civilian migration is counted only when at least one reserved settler is observed in gl-island-migration-zone; an empty hull at another shore cannot produce false success, and a wrong-zone landing is adopted only after a current natural resource is found on the settlers' actual zone.

The landed settlers receive a refreshed resource task and request the matching drop site: Mining Camp for gold or stone, Lumber Camp for trees, and Mill for forage or prey; when affordable, placement tries no more than four bounded offsets and ordinary home placement cannot satisfy the colony's acceptance record.

If no migration launches on an expired timer, at most five gate snapshots distinguish the engine-idle-villager bucket, available Transport Ship count, home-defense state, global-depletion state, and the sum of competing transport-controller states.

After a resource-bearing colony is confirmed and resources-depleted is YES on RIVERS, ISLANDS, or TEAM-ISLANDS, gather percentages retain nonzero wood, gold, and stone demand and migrated settlers continue working the remote resource in the fresh replay.

A wrong-zone landing on a resource-free islet is stopped and released rather than falsely counted, but the engine provides no reliable second-hop path query and those settlers are not yet automatically recovered to another island.

A matching drop site that is temporarily unaffordable waits for the migration watchdog rather than consuming four meaningless coordinate retries; fresh replay telemetry must distinguish that resource wait from point rejection.

gl-island-colony-established is set only after the owned drop-site foundation is accepted, but it is not yet cleared automatically if every settler dies or that remote colony later exhausts its resources; per-zone colony lifecycle evidence remains unavailable.

resources-depleted remains a global known-map signal rather than a home-island depletion measure; the independent two-idle-villager trigger handles visible shoreline unemployment, while a per-land-zone resource inventory and per-zone gather allocation remain unresolved.
